mainEntity.name: How often should wiper blades be replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most blades are worn out somewhere between six and twelve months in Sydney conditions, and cars parked outside sit at the shorter end of that. Rather than working to a calendar, check the rubber edge with a fingertip every few months: smooth and slightly soft is fine, ridged or hard means replace them.

mainEntity.name: Can I just replace the rubber insert instead of the whole blade?

acceptedAnswer.text: On some conventional blades you can, and on beam blades you generally cannot because the rubber and the spring spine are made as one unit. Refills also assume the frame and its claws are still in good order. If the frame is corroded or a claw has lost its grip, a fresh insert will still wipe badly.

mainEntity.name: Do the front blades have to be the same length?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Many vehicles run a longer blade on the driver's side than the passenger's, because the sweep patterns are different. Fitting two of the same length is a common mistake and it either leaves an unwiped band or lets the blades clash at the top of the sweep. We match each side to the vehicle specification.

mainEntity.name: Why do my wipers judder even though the blades are new?

acceptedAnswer.text: Juddering on new blades points to something other than the rubber. The usual causes are a contaminated windscreen that needs a proper clean, arms that have lost spring tension, or an arm sitting at the wrong angle so the blade cannot flip cleanly. Check all three before buying another set.

mainEntity.name: Can you replace wipers while you are doing other glass work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is the sensible time to do it. The wiper arms come off during a windscreen replacement anyway, and fitting worn blades back onto brand new glass is a quick way to mark the screen. Tell us when you book and we will bring the blades with the glass.

mainEntity.name: Do you do rear wipers as well?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Rear blades are a separate part with their own length and fitting type, and easy to overlook because you only notice them in the wet. Mention it when you book so we bring the right one.
